notes: Works of art approved for city buildings in the narrative Art Commission minutes of 1934-1941: the Public Works of Art Project murals of 1934 (Coit Tower, the Mother's House, the Board of Education room, Roosevelt, Balboa and John Muir schools), the George Washington High School frescoes and frieze, Mission High and Beach Chalet murals, City Hall and City College works, and the Coit Tower complaint of 1941. Found by searching for mural, fresco, mosaic, frieze and sculpture passages. Artists are named as the makers of the work, not as occupants.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: Lafayette School lunette by William Gaskin (1934; which Lafayette School building is unclear), Sherman School lobby murals by Jay Risling (1936, sent back for restudy), Piazzoni's mural for the Morgue (1936, in a building since replaced), Maynard Dixon's four murals for Presidio High School (1937, no page), the Spreckels Lake model yacht club mosaics (1938), and the 1938-39 Golden Gate International Exposition works on Treasure Island.
coverage.note: Passages found with an ad hoc search; the curated list is /mnt/project-files/sf-art-commission/F5.py.

findings.address_as_written: Coit Tower vestibule and lower floor, Public Works of Art Project sketches
findings.description: The Art Commission tentatively approved the first Public Works of Art Project sketches for Coit Tower: four panels and two small lunettes in oil for the vestibule by Cuneo, Gaw, Del Pino and Oldfield, and frescoes for the lower floor by George Harris, Victor Arnautoff, Suzanne Scheuer, Ray Bertrand, William Hesthal, Fred Vidar and Ben Cunningham, some of them sent back for restudy. It asked to see each work again when the drawings were on the wall and when it was finished.
